system_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Analyze the provided codebase for bugs, security issues, and correctness problems. Provide actionable feedback. All files are located in /tmp/files
task_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Your task is to analyze the jmxterm codebase. jmxterm is a command-line JMX client that connects to MBean servers, runs commands (open, close, get, set, run, beans, domain, etc.), and handles file/stream I/O, session state, and JDK-specific process discovery. The codebase handles command parsing and chaining, JMX connection lifecycle, MBean attribute and operation invocation, notification subscription, and URL resolution (host:port and PID). Your goal is to identify bugs, correctness issues, boundary condition errors, logic errors, off-by-one mistakes, missing validation checks, resource leaks, and any other issues that could affect reliability or correctness. Focus on: control flow in command chaining and short-circuit behavior, connection and session lifecycle (connect/disconnect/close), null checks and guards before API calls, use of getConnection() vs isConnected() when checking session state, executor and scheduler lifecycle in watch/report mode, exception handling in close() and flush(), and regex patterns for URL/host parsing. Write your findings to /tmp/outputs/review.md

rubric.criterion: Identifies that in CommandCenter.doExecute(String command) in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/cc/CommandCenter.java the loop over &&-delimited command segments does not short-circuit: all segments are executed even when execute(c) returns false, so a failing command in the chain does not prevent later commands from running

Identifies the missing null check in GetCommand.displayAttributes() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/cmd/GetCommand.java: after BeanCommand.getBeanName(bean, domain, session) the code calls new ObjectName(beanName) without guarding against null beanName, which can throw when bean resolves to null (e.g. isNull(bean))

Identifies that in FileCommandOutput.close() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/io/FileCommandOutput.java fileWriter.flush() is called followed by fileWriter.close() without try/finally, so if flush() throws an exception close() is never called and the file writer is left open

Identifies that in ValueFormat.parseValue() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/utils/ValueFormat.java the code strips surrounding double quotes using charAt(0) and charAt(length-1) without first checking that value.length() >= 2, so a single-character or empty string is parsed incorrectly

Identifies that in Jdk9JavaProcess.startManagementAgent() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/jdk9/Jdk9JavaProcess.java the VM obtained from attach() is never detached in a finally block, causing a resource leak when startLocalManagementAgent or casting throws

Identifies that WriterCommandOutput in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/io/WriterCommandOutput.java does not override close(), so when it wraps closeable Writers (e.g. FileWriter), calling close() on the CommandOutput never closes those writers, causing a resource leak

Identifies that in DomainsCommand.getCandidateDomains() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/cmd/DomainsCommand.java the error message passed to RuntimeIOException incorrectly spells "candate" instead of "candidate" (e.g. "Couldn't get candate domains")

Identifies that in BeanCommand.getBeanName() in src/main/java/org/cyclopsgroup/jmxterm/cmd/BeanCommand.java when bean.indexOf(':') != -1 the code catches InstanceNotFoundException with an empty catch and falls through, then unconditionally builds domainName + ":" + bean with no check that bean already contained ':', so a full MBean name that is not found gets the domain prepended again and produces a malformed name
